title: CSS Units: px vs rem vs em vs %
intro: Picking the right unit makes your layout scale nicely across screens and respect users' font settings.

slides.heading: px
slides.subtitle: A fixed size.
points: Same size regardless of the parent
Good for borders and fine details
Doesn't scale with the user's font settings

slides.heading: rem
slides.subtitle: Relative to the root font size.
points: 1rem equals the html font size (16px by default)
Scales when users change their browser font size
A great default for font sizes and spacing

slides.heading: em
slides.subtitle: Relative to the parent's font size.
points: Handy for padding that scales with text

slides.heading: % and vw / vh
slides.subtitle: Relative to a container or the screen.
points: % is relative to the parent element

scenario.situation: A user with low vision sets their browser's default font size to 24px.
scenario.problem: Your site uses font-size: 14px everywhere, so the text stays tiny and hard to read.
scenario.fix: Switch font sizes to rem (14px becomes 0.875rem). The text now scales with the user's setting.
scenario.takeaway: Use rem for text so it respects user preferences.
